aliases: Remote Authentication Dial In User Service

first_operational.notes: RFC 2058 says RADIUS was originally developed by Livingston for the PortMaster series; exact pre-RFC release date remains to be recovered.

roles: centralize authentication and service configuration for dispersed serial-line/modem-pool access servers
allow a Network Access Server to act as a client of shared authentication/authorization servers
return extensible service attributes controlling PPP, SLIP, Telnet, LAT, IP and other access services
addressing: RADIUS attributes can carry framed IP address/netmask and NAS identity/port data; exact attribute set is RFC-generation dependent.
routing_or_forwarding: RADIUS itself does not forward subscriber traffic; it returns authorization/configuration used by the NAS to establish services such as routed/framed IP access.
error_control: Application-level request retransmission/failover over UDP rather than TCP transport reliability.

operations.monitoring: NAS/server transactions and attributes provide access-control state; later accounting is a related protocol branch.
operations.diagnostics: Access-Reject/Challenge/response handling and server failover are operational concerns; implementation logs remain to be excavated.
operations.remote_management: Central server database/policy separates account/service configuration from individual NAS boxes.
operations.failure_behavior: NAS retries/fails over among configured RADIUS servers when requests are not answered; exact retry behavior varies by implementation/version.
operations.operator_interface: Server user/client/dictionary configuration files and NAS RADIUS configuration; pre-RFC Livingston formats remain to be recovered.

open_questions: Locate the pre-RFC Livingston RADIUS source tree and first shipping release.

Diff RFC 2058, RFC 2138 and RFC 2865 packet/security/attribute semantics.
Trace later 802.1X/EAP, Wi-Fi, VPN and device-administration uses as separate adoption branches rather than original requirements.

Product/manual context predating the RFC publication.
